newsitem.title: PERU: Peru guerrillas' deadline passes without incident.
newsitem.headline: Peru guerrillas' deadline passes without incident.

text.p: Peruvian guerrillas holding at least 200 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima allowed a deadline to pass on Wednesday without carrying out their threat to kill Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela.

Rebel spokesmen appeared to scale down their immediate demands by not repeating calls for President Alberto Fujimori's presence. They asked instead for medicine to treat wounded guerrillas and hostages.
Ten minutes before the 12:20 p.m. (1720 GMT) deadline, rebels released four elderly male hostages, according to witnesses and Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) members.
"Until they bring us medicines, no other hostage is going to get out," one of the MRTA spokesmen said.
Without setting a deadline, the rebels have threatened to kill all the hostages if the government does not release an estimated 400 to 500 MRTA prisoners and transported them to the jungle.
